conviction_note: The reported quarter is already public ($222.7m YUTREPIA sales and $396.1m cash, pre-announced 13 Oct), so the print turns on management's first post-settlement read of PAH-only demand and whether the reaffirmed >$1bn 2027 ambition survives losing PH-ILD, which was about half of patients. Two things favour the long side: UTHR said on 4 Nov that it expects only moderate near-term switching back from YUTREPIA, and the short position is crowded (17.3m shares on 15 Oct, about 19% of shares outstanding, up 4.7m in two weeks). Against that: a +74% 20-day run-up, put skew of +15.6 vol points, a likely GAAP loss from accruing the settlement in Q3, and a probable reset of the 2027 ambition. Net is close to balanced, so p_up 52 on an abs move of 11 (scaled +0.44). That sits beside a findings sum of +0.5, the same sign and size by coincidence, not by fitting.
bar: Revenue was pre-released at $222.7m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001819576/000110465926115672/tm2627557d1_ex99-1.htm, 2026-10-13). The consensus is disputed: Chartmill ~$218.5m revenue / $0.98 EPS (search snippet, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/LQDA/estimates), Earnings Whispers $186.6m / $0.77 (stale, pre-dates the pre-announcement; https://finviz.com/news/414618/liquidias-halved-stock-sets-a-low-bar-as-eutrepia-launch-faces-its-toughest-test, 2026-11-03), Benzinga $195.7-204.7m / $0.94 (snippet). print_vs_bar uses Chartmill (+1.9%); against Earnings Whispers it would be +19%. The bar that matters is forward: the company's own reaffirmed ambition of >$1bn 2027 net revenue, set before the settlement (per the Earnings Whispers preview above). No consensus for Q4 or 2027 after the settlement was found. Because the bar is disputed, every size is capped small.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest was 17,303,701 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, up 4,662,980 from 30 Sep (12.64m), about 19.3% of shares outstanding, 1.98 days to cover; the Oct-30 figure is due 10 Nov (https://equibles.com/stocks/lqda/shortinterest, read 2026-11-09; massive.com corroborates 17.3m / 2.0 days, https://massive.com/quote/lqda). This is a crowded short that built into the settlement rally. From the baseline: 25-delta skew +15.57 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.56, ATM spread 78% of mid (implied move indicative only), run-up +73.9% over 20 days and +15.0% over 5 days, 47% below the 52-week high. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits went bearish to neutral on 13 Oct (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/lqda-explodes-after-hours-on-deal-ending-years-of-patent-fight-keeping-yutrepia-on-market/cZxBUFeRBYs).

findings.finding: PH-ILD was about half of YUTREPIA use ('equal scripting between PAH and PH-ILD', patient mix 'pretty balanced, 50-50' on the Q1 2026 call). The company had reaffirmed a >$1bn 2027 net revenue ambition before the 13-Oct settlement forced it to stop promoting for PH-ILD and file to remove the indication. This print is management's first chance to restate or withdraw that number, and to give Q4 and 2027 run-rate commentary. A withdrawal, or a 2027 figure well below $1bn, is the likely negative line. The release of 13 Oct said only that a 'broader update on YUTREPIA performance' would come on this call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: LQDA has never given formal revenue guidance; its forward commentary moved it +25.6% (May 2026, beat plus raised targets) and -10.5% (Aug 2026, sell-off after Q2). The PH-ILD ruling itself moved it -57% on 1 Oct and -14% the next day, and the settlement +40% on 14 Oct.
findings.why_not_priced: The PH-ILD exposure is public, and the stock fell from about $62 to $26.6 when it was lost, so most of it is priced. What is not priced is management's own quantification. If the market had already priced a large 2027 reset, sell-side targets would not have been raised to $58-70 after the settlement (HCW $65, BTIG $70), and the stock would not be up 74% in 20 days.
findings.independence: The 2027 >$1bn ambition is in the Earnings Whispers preview, a different document (https://finviz.com/news/414618/liquidias-halved-stock-sets-a-low-bar-as-eutrepia-launch-faces-its-toughest-test, 2026-11-03). The required label removal is in the company's 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001819576/000110465926115672/tm2627557d1_8k.htm). The UTHR finding below is evidence on the same retention question from the opposite side, so the two net against each other.

findings.finding: United Therapeutics, the direct competitor and settlement counterparty, reported on 4 Nov, after Liquidia last spoke. Management said it expects only 'moderate near-term switching back' from YUTREPIA. It also reported record Tyvaso revenue of $504m, Tyvaso DPI up 13%, referrals over 1,000 in October, and said that competitive therapies still hurt DPI sales in the quarter. Read for Liquidia, existing PH-ILD patients look largely retained near term (the label change still awaits FDA approval), which supports a Q4 run-rate above a straight halving.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior instance of a competitor's read on patient retention. LQDA rose from $41.85 on 3 Nov to about $48 on 9 Nov (+15% in 5 days), which straddles UTHR's 4 Nov release.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the +15% five-day run-up after 3 Nov is most of what this would buy. The rest is that the comment is an interpretation in UTHR's call coverage, not a number. Liquidia will put a number on it, and a retention figure near UTHR's 'moderate' would confirm that the stock's recovery was justified, not stretched.
findings.independence: UTHR's own release (https://investingnews.com/united-therapeutics-corporation-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results/, 2026-11-04) confirms that 'competitive therapies negatively impacted sales' of Tyvaso DPI, which means YUTREPIA was still taking share in Q3. The 'moderate switching back' wording appears only in the Earnings Whispers / finviz summary and a search snippet of other coverage.

findings.finding: The Delaware ruling that the '327 PH-ILD claims are valid and infringed came on 30 Sep, the last day of the quarter, and the $380.7m net settlement followed on 13 Oct. That makes the litigation loss probable and estimable at quarter end, so Q3 GAAP results will likely accrue the settlement as a Type I subsequent event. That would turn a consensus of $0.77-0.98 EPS into a large GAAP net loss, around -$3 a share if the full amount is expensed. This is my inference from ASC 450/855: the company has not stated its accounting treatment.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On EPS misses: in Q2 2026, EPS of $0.74 missed $0.81 and the stock fell -10.5%. In March 2026 an EPS miss came with a +8.3% move on upgrades (https://www.trefis.com/stock/lqda/articles/593169/liquidia-stock-8-3-analyst-upgrades-media-praise-overpower-eps-miss/2026-03-11).
findings.why_not_priced: The dollars are known and the cash cost is in the price. The only unpriced part is a headline 'EPS miss' if consensus feeds leave the settlement out, and EPS consensus figures of $0.77-0.98 suggest they do. It is below operating income with no path to the guide, so it is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: none (my accounting inference from the dates in the 8-K)

findings.finding: Short interest rose to 17.3m shares at the 15 Oct settlement, about 19% of shares outstanding, up 4.66m (+37%) from 30 Sep and close to its 2-year high. Days to cover is only about 2.0 at the elevated volume. So a large short position was built at roughly $27-40, and the stock has since run to $48. If management's PAH-only outlook or retention data is not clearly worse than feared, the covering is a mechanism inside the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Two of the last three prints moved more than 10% (+25.6%, -10.5%). The settlement gap on 14 Oct (+40%, after-hours +51%) came with short interest of about 12.6m.
findings.why_not_priced: The +74% run-up says some covering has already happened. The Oct-30 figure (due 10 Nov) is unknown, and Equibles' model expects about 17.6m. If the short had fully covered, the put skew would not still be +15.6 vol points and days to cover would not be rising.
findings.independence: https://massive.com/quote/lqda (17.3m, 2.0 days, Oct 15). The Sep-30 figure of 12.64m comes from a separate quote page cited in a search snippet.

findings.finding: Cash was $396.1m at 30 Sep. Against it, $60.3m was due to Sandoz/Henderson/PBM around 16 Oct, $175m net to UTHR by about 24 Nov, and $72.7m each on 31 Jan and 30 Apr 2027. The HCR revenue-interest amendment raised the minimum cash covenant from $15m to $45m, and the company arranged a third-party letter of credit. Management said it will fund the payments from sales and cash 'without requiring additional financing'. Asking what money would buy: it would buy a settlement, not a ramp. A raise announced with results after a +74% run-up is possible but is contradicted by management's own statement, so this is a small negative tail.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline. The company raised equity in earlier years (quantisnow headline on a $67.5m common stock financing, undated in the snippet).
findings.why_not_priced: Most of it is priced: the cash schedule is public. What is not priced is the probability of an opportunistic raise. If the market expected one, the stock would not have run 15% in the five days before the print.
findings.independence: The management quote is in the ex99-1 press release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001819576/000110465926115672/tm2627557d1_ex99-1.htm), which is the same filing as the 8-K.

findings.finding: Q3 YUTREPIA net sales of $222.7m were pre-announced, up 31% from Q2's $170.4m. Some consensus feeds still carry stale bars (Earnings Whispers $186.6m, Benzinga $195.7-204.7m), so the release may print as a headline revenue 'beat' of 9-19% against those feeds, but only about +2% against Chartmill's $218.5m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats: $171.7m vs $167.8m in Q2 2026 was sold (-10.5%); Q1 2026 was bought (+25.6%).
findings.why_not_priced: The number itself is priced, since it was pre-released. Only the headline mechanics against stale feeds are not, so the size is near zero.
findings.independence: Q2 base of $170.4m from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001819576/000110465926094411/tm2622888d1_ex99-1.htm)

outside_window.finding: The FDA decision on the label supplement removing PH-ILD has uncertain timing, and the settlement releases only take effect once the FDA approves the label change. Payer coverage of off-label PH-ILD use after the label changes is the real revenue cliff, and it falls after the exit window unless management dates it on the call.
The $175m net payment to UTHR is due within 30 business days of 13 Oct (about 24 Nov 2026), and the $72.7m installments on 31 Jan and 30 Apr 2027.

baseline_tension: The skew (+15.6 vol points downside paid) and the +74% 20-day run-up both argue for a give-back. My positive pieces (crowded short, UTHR's 'moderate switching back') cut against the skew, and the guidance-reset and GAAP-loss pieces agree with it. The net is barely positive, and p_up sits at 52, not higher, for that reason.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): the guidance-reset negative went from -1.0 to -0.8 because short interest is about 19% of shares outstanding and rising.
Rules 1/3 (partly priced, own caveat): the UTHR read-through went from +1.0 to +0.8 because the +15% five-day run-up already straddles UTHR's 4 Nov release.
Rule 2 (one-off below operating income): the GAAP settlement accrual went from -0.5 to -0.3, since it has no path to the guide and rests on my accounting inference.
Rule 6 / core table (pre-released line, disputed bar): the reported-quarter headline beat went from +0.2 to +0.1.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): kept at -0.3 after asking what money would buy (a settlement, not a ramp) and noting management's 'no additional financing' statement.
Rule 8 (understatement): abs_move raised from the 6.77 option figure to 11, given the recent print reactions (25.6, 10.5, 13.7), 113% realised vol and a first post-settlement outlook.
